Oliver — thanks, great summary. Quick answers and the MAP action list below. I attached our plan and a short readme for test accounts.

High-level: Redwood will run two validation phases in the MAP — a controlled profiling run (low-concurrency, instrumented) and a full load run (target concurrency, sustained for 30m windows). Goal: produce TTFT, p50/p90/p99 token latency, and overall tokens/sec.

What you get from Redwood for the tests:
- Scoped test API keys (scoped to the sandbox project) with a 14-day expiry. Keys are read-only for logs/observability and full for inference — we'll send separate keys for profiling vs load.
- A benchmark playbook (attached) with the exact command lines we use, sample scripts, and the k8s job manifest for the load driver.
- Two sets of recommended windows (PDT): pre-prod evenings 02:00–04:00 (PDT) and weekend long-run Saturday 04:00–08:00 (PDT). Please confirm preferred dates.

Proposed MAP milestones (short):
1) Access & smoke — issue keys, confirm endpoint reachability (48 hours)
2) Profiling run — up to 8 concurrent sessions, instrumenting for per-token latency (2 business days)
3) Full-load runs — target concurrencies 8 / 16 / 32 / 64, 30m sustained windows, collect traces and KV cache metrics (3 days)
4) Analysis & report — consolidated p50/p90/p99, TTFT matrix, cost projection and recommended config (2 business days)
5) Close decision — sign-off and procurement handoff

Attachments I sent: datascale-map-benchmark-plan-v1.xlsx, benchmark-load-windows.csv, test-accounts-readme.txt

Next steps from you: confirm which of the two windows (weekday evenings vs weekend) you prefer and list any additional IP allowlist entries for the sandbox. Once we have that I will loop in Monica and Vivek for run ownership.

Thanks —

Looping in run plan details. Key technical notes for the profiling and load windows:

- Profiling: we will run deterministic prompts (10k tokens/session, same seed) to isolate model kernel variance. Collect KV cache hit/miss and GPU util at 1s granularity.
- Full load: use synthetic fanout driver with adjustable think-time. Recommend target session ramp schedule: 0→target over 5m, sustain 30m, cool-down 10m. Repeat for each concurrency step.
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured from request accept to first token byte out; include warm vs cold start buckets.
- Concurrency mix: suggest 80% short sessions (<=2k tokens) and 20% long sessions (10k tokens) to reflect DataScale's profile.
- Abort criteria: if token p99 latency > 5s or GPU OOM observed, abort and collect traces for triage.

I'll prepare the exact k6 and python-runner commands and attach quick-run scripts by EOD. We're OK to use the 02:00–04:00 PDT weekday slot on April 20 if that works for DataScale.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
